title: A piece with no English paragraph fails with the desk's own sentence
body:
## Summary
analysePiece threw NOT_ENGLISH_LINE as a plain Error, so the failed reading showed the generic analyse line and was classed unknown.

## Description
desk/src/lib/desk/essay.ts:223 threw `new Error(NOT_ENGLISH_LINE)` when every paragraph was not English. desk/src/lib/desk/job.ts:91-96 jobError keeps a message only for DeskSaid, so the session job and the TV caption (desk/src/essay/EssayTV.tsx:221 shows job.error) read "The desk could not read that through.", and job.ts:80 failureOf classed it unknown (retryable). The phone's piece door refuses such a piece before any run (desk/src/app/api/analyse/route.ts:176) but the Workroom shelf-piece door (route.ts:158-168) does not, and /api/texts (desk/src/app/api/texts/route.ts:66) keeps any text, so a kept Czech piece reaches analysePiece. Registry: error-handling / structured-propagation and taxonomy-design (the category is decided at birth). Fixed: the throw is a DeskSaid.

## Flow
- Keep a Czech piece on the shelf from the phone (texts POST)
- Workroom Read it on the TV -> analyse kind shelf-piece -> analysePiece: every paragraph notEnglish -> plain Error
- Before: Not read caption "The desk could not read that through."; after: the NOT_ENGLISH_LINE sentence, failure said

## Expected impact
A learner whose kept piece is not in English is told why on the TV instead of a generic failure. Could break: nothing reads the old generic text for this case (essay-piece-test's /not in English/ rejection still holds).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the failure carries the desk's reason
Before: jobError(analyse, e) = "The desk could not read that through.", failureOf = unknown (new essay-rules-test case red, exit 1)
After: jobError = NOT_ENGLISH_LINE, failureOf = said, no model call (exit 0)
Method: gate - red-then-green rules test on the real change
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/desk/essay.ts:223 (before): throw lastError ?? new Error(notEnglish.length ? NOT_ENGLISH_LINE : ...)
desk/src/lib/desk/job.ts:92 if (e instanceof DeskSaid) return e.message;
desk/src/app/api/analyse/route.ts:166 shelf-piece -> readPiece with no English pre-check (piece door: route.ts:176)
tools/essay-rules-test.cjs red: actual "The desk could not read that through."

title: The worked idea is asked through the prompt assembler (ledger names the prompt)
body:
## Summary
teachTopic built its prompt by hand, so its metered rows carried prompt null - the only text family in lib/desk off the assembler.

## Description
desk/src/lib/desk/worked.ts:46-50 called text() with a hand-built system and prompt; desk/src/lib/engines/call.ts:49 meters `prompt: req.fingerprint`, which only lib/prompt/assemble.ts sets, so worked-idea ledger rows could not be tied to a prompt version (desk/src/lib/engines/meter.ts:18 "null for a family not yet on the assembler"). Registry: prompt-assembly / fingerprinting-and-cache-keys ("tracing a behavior shift to the prompt version that caused it"). Fixed: four say() parts joined by a newline, the same bytes, now fingerprinted; the engines ratchet tools/prompt-assembly-test.cjs BY_HAND lowered (coupled).

## Flow
- teachTopic -> text({system, prompt}) with no fingerprint -> meter row prompt null
- Fix: assemble("worked-idea", ...) and spread it into the call
- A wording change to the idea prompt now moves its fingerprint on the ledger

## Expected impact
Whoever reads the usage ledger can attribute a worked-idea quality or cost shift to its prompt version. Could break: nothing; the prompt text is pinned unchanged by the new test.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every desk text family is traceable on the ledger
Before: fingerprint undefined (worked-rules-test red, exit 1); text families in lib/desk on the assembler 10 of 11; hand-assembled calls in the tree 9
After: 12-hex fingerprint, stable per topic, prompt bytes unchanged (exit 0); 11 of 11; 8
Method: gate - red-then-green test plus the ratchet's own red until its pin was lowered
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/desk/worked.ts:46 (before) text({ system: withManner(...), prompt: `Topic: ...`, use: "worked-idea" })
desk/src/lib/engines/call.ts:49 meter({ ..., prompt: req.fingerprint, ... })
tools/prompt-assembly-test.cjs:85 'src/lib/desk/worked.ts':1 (removed)

title: The retry route's kind list is checked against the runJob calls that hold an input
body:
## Summary
POST /api/session/retry's ROUTES map is a hand list that must cover every job kind a route runs with an input; no test derived it, and it drifted once.

## Description
desk/src/app/api/session/retry/route.ts:165-170 ROUTES = read, hint, practice, teach. The phone (desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:421) and the TV offer Try again on any failed job with `input` and retry !== false; a kind with an input but no ROUTES entry answers NOTHING (409). This gap was real on 2026-10-13 (B card "a failed lesson (teach) holds its input but Try again cannot reach it"). SKILL 4.7: the test now derives the population from the source - every comment-stripped runJob call under desk/src with an input - and asserts each is a ROUTES key, with a canary for the scanner. Registry: job-coordination / terminal-state-recovery.

## Flow
- Add a job kind whose route passes input to runJob, forget ROUTES
- Before: phone offers Try again, retry 409 "There is nothing to try again"; no test notices
- After: desk-jobs-rules-test names the missing kind

## Expected impact
Developers adding a pipeline get a red suite instead of a dead Try again button. Could break: a runJob call written in an unusual shape could escape the scanner (the canary pins the usual one).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a hand list is held to its ground truth
Before: 0 tests derive ROUTES; seeded (teach removed from ROUTES) the new case goes red naming teach, exit 1
After: 4 of 4 input-holding kinds (read, hint, practice, teach) checked, exit 0
Method: gate - instrument built, seeded control red, restored green
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The hint's ground asks commaSystem which systems get their notation line
body:
## Summary
hint.ts groundFor kept its own copy of the comma-system list after school.ts and kinds.ts moved to taskText commaSystem (hand-off from maths-school 87603d8f).

## Description
desk/src/lib/desk/hint.ts:138 tested `who.system === "cz" || who.system === "de"`; desk/src/lib/rules/taskText.ts:56 commaSystem is the one authority (87603d8f moved school.ts and kinds.ts to it; calc2.ts keeps its own by its seam rule). A third comma system would be read and marked as one but its hints never told its notation. Fixed: groundFor asks commaSystem; a comment-stripped source scan with its canary pins it.

## Flow
- A new comma system is added to commaSystem
- Before: hint groundFor omits its notationLine; after: carries it
- cz/de still get notationLine, uk/us nothing (pinned)

## Expected impact
No behaviour change for the four systems today; one rule, one place. hint.ts is on the live surface: a drift record is owed before merge.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one authority for the comma-system rule
Before: 1 inline copy in this context (maths-rules-test scan red, exit 1)
After: 0 (exit 0); groundFor output unchanged for cz, de, uk, us
Method: gate - red-then-green source scan plus behaviour asserts
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/desk/hint.ts:138 (before) if (who.system === "cz" || who.system === "de") parts.push(notationLine(who.system));
desk/src/lib/rules/taskText.ts:56 export const commaSystem = (system?: SchoolSystem) => system === "cz" || system === "de";

title: A photo over the read cap is refused on the mark door too, before any run
body:
## Summary
/api/read caps a phone photo at READ_IMAGE_MAX; /api/mark took the same kind of photo with no cap and handed it to a job and the vision engine.

## Description
desk/src/app/api/read/route.ts:32 refuses through rules/maths readImageProblem (desk/src/lib/rules/maths.ts:125-129, 12 MB as a data URL, built 2026-10-13). desk/src/app/api/mark/route.ts:57-59 checked only that the image was non-empty, for both the set mark and the page mark. Fixed: the one cap right after, before any job. The read door's cap had no test either; the new case pins all three doors.

## Flow
- Paired phone posts a 12 MB + 1 data URL to /api/mark with a set on the desk
- Before: 200, a mark job, one vision call
- After: 400 with the read's sentence, no job, no vision call; a normal photo still marks

## Expected impact
A malformed or hostile client cannot push an oversized photo to the vision engine through the mark door. Could break: a real photo over 12 MB, which the phone (1280 px JPEG 0.85) does not produce.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one cap on every photo door
Before: 1 of 2 photo doors capped; new desk-jobs-rules-test case red (200, one vision call), exit 1
After: 2 of 2; set mark and page mark 400, read pinned, normal photo 200 (exit 0)
Method: gate - red-then-green route test
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten

title: An embed outage opens the picked lesson at 0:00 and the TV never says so
instrument: a hint-route test with the embed provider failing (stub at the registry) asserting the session lesson carries degraded: true, plus a TV rows/caption test that the lesson card says it opened at the start
body:
## Summary
pickLesson drops bestWindow's degraded mark, so the session's LessonPick cannot tell the TV the lesson opened at its start because the search was down (hand-off from library 699112d3).

## Description
desk/src/lib/library/lessons.ts:116-130 now returns { t, text, score: 0, degraded: true } on an embed failure; desk/src/lib/desk/pick.ts:44-45 copies only t and text, and desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:94 LessonPick has no field for it. The learner sees the lesson start from 0:00 with no word that this is not the explaining bit (registry: error-handling / user-facing-mapping). Fix: carry degraded on LessonPick (session context), set it in pickLesson, and caption it on the TV lesson card (tv-surface/math-buddy). The type and the screen are outside this round's paths, hence B.

## Flow
- Embed engine down -> hint -> lesson job -> bestWindow degraded -> pickLesson drops the flag
- Fix order: LessonPick.degraded (store.ts), pickLesson sets it (pick.ts), TV caption reads it
- Pin with the instrument

## Expected impact
A learner told the desk could not find the exact bit, and the lesson starts from the beginning, instead of a silent 0:00. Could break: the lesson.set reducer's shape check if it whitelists fields.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the TV says when a lesson opens at its start for want of search
Before: pick.ts drops the flag on 1 of 1 degraded path (pick.ts:45)
After: the flag reaches the session and the TV caption (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked: embed down on build, on query, and a lesson with no vectors; the type and screen are outside this round, so no gate here
Result: better
Gate: none

body:
## Summary
A multi-paragraph piece with no English paragraph is refused, on the phone and the TV status, with the one-paragraph line.

## Description
desk/src/app/api/analyse/route.ts:176 (piece door) and desk/src/lib/desk/essay.ts:223 (analysePiece, now a DeskSaid) both say NOT_ENGLISH_LINE (desk/src/lib/rules/essay.ts:178): "This paragraph is not in English". The wording is pinned byte for byte by a council ruling (tools/essay-rules-test.cjs "E3-c guard: the refusal lines are byte for byte what they were at 3b97c46d"; tools/essay-piece-test.cjs:216-226 and 358), so changing it is the owner's call - escalation: direction (council-ruled copy).

## Flow
- Send a two-paragraph Czech piece from the phone
- Status and reply: "This paragraph is not in English..."
- Fix (if ruled): a piece line in rules/essay used by both piece sites

## Expected impact
A learner who sent a whole piece is told about the piece, not a paragraph. Could break: the council-pinned guard tests, by design.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the refusal names what was sent
Before: 2 of 2 piece sites say "This paragraph"
After: 0 of 2 (predicted with a piece line)
Method: probe - read the two sites and the pinned tests; not built because the wording is under a council guard
Result: better

title: The school draw's keep-a-spec loop is written three times in items.ts
instrument: an experiment script that snapshots makeSchoolItems for every unit x mix x 50 seeds x aim/paper/topSlips on the base tree, then on the change, and diffs them (0 differences expected)
body:
## Summary
Well formed, printed, leak-checked with no system, not already kept: the same keep rule is spelled in schoolSet, aimedSchoolDraw and aimTop.

## Description
desk/src/lib/desk/items.ts schoolSet's usual loop, aimedSchoolDraw and aimTop each repeat schoolWellFormed -> schoolQuestion(spec, system) -> leaksSchool(spec, schoolQuestion(spec)?.plain) -> sameKey dedupe, and two of them repeat the MB-B4 comment on why the leak check prints with no system. A fix to the keep rule (a new leak case) must land three times. One keepable(spec, system, seen) helper would hold it. Risk 4: the draws are seed-pinned and a reorder shifts every set, so it needs the whole-population snapshot first.

## Flow
- Count the keep-rule sites in items.ts
- Build the snapshot instrument on the base tree
- Extract the helper, re-run the snapshot, expect 0 differences

## Expected impact
A leak-check change lands once for every school draw. Could break: seeded sets if the extraction reorders a check.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one keep rule for the school draw
Before: 3 copies of the keep rule
After: 1 (predicted), 0 set differences on the snapshot
Method: simulation - three draws walked; the population snapshot is the instrument and exceeds this round
Result: better
Gate: none

desk/src/lib/desk/items.ts (schoolSet): if (!spec || !schoolWellFormed(spec).ok) continue; ... const q = schoolQuestion(spec, system); if (!q || leaksSchool(spec, schoolQuestion(spec)?.plain)) continue;

title: A snapped page's title has no cap before the learner file
instrument: a read-route test posting a 1 MB title with a small image: Before the history label is 1 MB long; After it is bounded - the owner's cut-versus-replace choice decides how
body:
## Summary
/api/read takes any string as the page title and writes it to the session page and the learner's history label.

## Description
desk/src/app/api/read/route.ts:26 keeps body.title when it is a non-blank string; route.ts:58 writes it as the history label (learners.json) and the page carries it in session.json. Every other learner text on these routes is capped (hint question, transcript, typed answers; the essay task is cut at 400 in desk/src/app/api/analyse/route.ts:55). The phone sends short sample-derived titles (desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:265), so only a crafted paired client reaches it. Whether an over-long title is cut or replaced by "Page" is a product choice, hence B with the instrument named.

## Flow
- Paired client posts /api/read with title = 1 MB string
- Page and history label hold 1 MB
- Fix: a title cap in rules, cut or replaced before the run

## Expected impact
The learner file stays bounded. Could break: nothing the phone sends.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every learner text on the pipeline routes is bounded
Before: title unbounded on 1 of 1 read door
After: bounded (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked the route; the cut-vs-replace choice is open, so not built
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
desk/src/app/api/read/route.ts:26 title: typeof body.title === "string" && body.title.trim() ? body.title : "Page"
desk/src/app/api/read/route.ts:58 withHistory(getLearner(owner), { at, kind: "homework", label: title, ... })

title: The agent-memory deviation on this context is stale: notes now carry time and source
body:
## Summary
.ai/registry-map.json records desk-pipelines x agent-memory as a deviation (memory.ts:87, no provenance), judged against a digest the subject has moved past.

## Description
The map row's evaluatedAgainst sha256-b2:4f054116d66a9495 differs from the subject's digest sha256-b2:7770d30ff5df3c25, so the verdict is stale. Its evidence says notes are "appended as plain strings without provenance"; desk/src/lib/desk/memory.ts:118 now writes { text, at, source: "nightly" } (observation-clock), and notesPart (memory.ts:42-48) frames them as unchecked, dated data. Supersedence is still absent. The verdict needs a re-judge by /conform --stale, which writes the shared map: an operator-only act (escalation), not a round-agent's.

## Flow
- Read the registry-map pair for desk-pipelines x agent-memory
- Compare its evidence with memory.ts:115-119
- Run /conform --stale on the pair

## Expected impact
The map stops claiming a provenance gap that was closed, and records the one that is left (supersedence). Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the recorded verdict matches the code
Before: verdict deviation, stale (digest moved), evidence cites a gap partly closed
After: a fresh verdict from /conform (not taken here)
Method: probe - read the pair and the code; the verdict itself is /conform's to write; rung failed: the instrument is the shared map, owned by the director
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
.ai/registry-map.json desk-pipelines agent-memory: state deviation, evaluatedAgainst sha256-b2:4f054116d66a9495, digest sha256-b2:7770d30ff5df3c25
desk/src/lib/desk/memory.ts:118 saveLearner({ ...l, memory: [...l.memory, ...lines.map((text) => ({ text, at, source: "nightly" }))] })
